control_name: URL Request Path Canonicalization Before Authorization
description: Ensure the web server, reverse proxy, or application framework canonicalizes request URIs — resolving path equivalences (., ..), stripping matrix parameters (;param=value), normalizing percent-encoding, collapsing duplicate slashes, and standardizing trailing slashes — before the authorization module evaluates access control rules. The root cause of CWE-551 is a behavior ordering defect where authorization sees a raw URI form that does not match configured security constraints, but the routing/dispatch layer later normalizes the URI and matches a protected resource. Canonicalization-first ensures the authorization decision and the routing decision operate on the same resolved path. Implementation varies by stack: Spring Security's StrictHttpFirewall rejects non-normalized requests; Tomcat's encodedSolidusHandling and allowBackslash settings control normalization; Nginx's merge_slashes and location matching normalize by default; Apache's AllowEncodedSlashes and mod_rewrite handle encoding normalization. Reverse proxies should be configured to normalize before forwarding to backends, and frameworks should reject requests containing path-equivalent sequences rather than silently normalizing them.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Attacker can no longer bypass authorization using non-canonical URL forms (matrix parameters, double encoding, path segment equivalences, trailing characters); exploitation requires finding a bypass that survives full URI canonicalization before the authorization decision evaluates the request

verification.method: Test that non-canonical URL forms (matrix parameters, dot-segments, encoded path separators) do not bypass authorization on protected endpoints; inspect web server and framework configuration for canonicalization-before-auth settings

commands.expected: 401 or 403 — matrix parameter does not bypass auth
401 or 403 — dot-segment does not bypass auth
401 or 403 — encoded dot does not bypass auth

remediation.name: Nginx path canonicalization and traversal rejection via drop-in config

steps.description: Create an Nginx drop-in config that explicitly enables merge_slashes and rejects requests containing path traversal sequences (dot-segments, encoded path separators, matrix parameters)
Add a rejection block to the server context that returns 400 for flagged requests (add this inside each server {} block or a shared include)
steps.command: printf '# Include inside server {} blocks:\n# if ($cme921_block) { return 400; }\n' >> /etc/nginx/conf.d/cme-921-canonicalization.conf

steps.description: Reload Nginx to apply the new canonicalization rules

remediation.verify: grep -E 'merge_slashes|cme921_block' /etc/nginx/conf.d/cme-921-canonicalization.conf && curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'http://localhost/./admin/' | grep -qE '^(400|403)$' && echo 'PASS: non-canonical paths rejected'

remediation.name: Apache HTTPD path canonicalization via AllowEncodedSlashes and mod_rewrite

steps.description: Create an Apache drop-in config that prevents encoded slash decoding and rejects requests containing path traversal sequences via mod_rewrite
steps.command:
printf '# CME-921: URL path canonicalization before authorization
AllowEncodedSlashes NoDecode

RewriteEngine On
# Reject dot-segment traversal sequences
RewriteCond %%{REQUEST_URI} (\.\.) [OR]
RewriteCond %%{REQUEST_URI} (%%2[eE]\.) [OR]
RewriteCond %%{REQUEST_URI} (\.%%2[eE]) [OR]
# Reject matrix parameters that could bypass path matching
RewriteCond %%{REQUEST_URI} (;[^/]*=)
RewriteRule .* - [F]
' > /etc/httpd/conf.d/cme-921-canonicalization.conf

steps.description: Reload Apache to apply the new canonicalization rules

remediation.verify: grep -E 'AllowEncodedSlashes|RewriteCond.*2[eE]' /etc/httpd/conf.d/cme-921-canonicalization.conf && curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'http://localhost/./admin/' | grep -qE '^(400|403)$' && echo 'PASS: non-canonical paths rejected'
